Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, one of the clinicians who specializes in postpartum mental health here. Thank you for coming in—how are you feeling today?

I’ll be guiding you through a brief screening called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS. It’s a simple set of 10 questions that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally and physically in the week since your baby arrived. There’s no right or wrong answer; we just want to make sure we’re giving you the best support possible.

Everything we discuss stays confidential within your care team, and this is a judgment-free zone. We’ll take it one question at a time, and you can answer in your own words—no need to worry about choosing from a list.

When you’re ready, let’s begin.  

First, in the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Um… not very often, honestly. I mean, maybe once or twice I’ve cracked a smile when my partner made a goofy face at the baby, but it feels kind of forced. Most of the time I’m just too worn-out or worried to find things funny.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, I guess that’s what I’m saying—I haven’t really been able to laugh much at all. It’s like the joy is kind of muted.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I mean, I try to look forward to things—like when my sister said she’d bring over coffee tomorrow—but even that feels kind of flat. I used to get excited about little plans, and now it’s more like I’m just getting through them.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… that happens a lot. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for, like, an hour, and I kept thinking it must be because I’m doing something wrong—maybe I’m not holding him right or my milk isn’t good enough. I know logically babies just cry, but I still feel it’s my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s going to choke, or I’ll lie down and picture him stopping breathing in the crib. There’s no real reason—it’s like my brain just spins these scary stories and I can’t shut them off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah, that too. Sometimes it hits out of nowhere—like I’ll be walking to change his diaper and suddenly feel this wave of terror, like something awful is about to happen. My chest gets tight, I can’t catch my breath, and I have to grip the crib rail until it passes. It’s over in a few minutes, but it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, honestly. It feels like the second I finish one thing—changing him, feeding him, trying to grab a bite myself—there’s already another thing waiting. The laundry piles up, the dishes sit there, and I keep thinking, “I can’t do all this.” I manage, but it’s like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I’ll lie down exhausted, but my head keeps circling all the “what-ifs” about the baby, or I replay every little thing I think I messed up. It takes me forever to drift off, and then I jerk awake at every squeak from the bassinet. I probably get three broken hours a night.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day. It’s like there’s this heavy cloud that won’t lift. I see the baby smile and I know I should feel happy, but mostly I just feel empty or on the verge of tears. Yesterday I cried while folding onesies because it felt like I’m failing him even when I’m trying so hard.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, that’s been happening. I broke down in the kitchen two days ago when the bottle warmer blinked wrong and I spilled milk everywhere. It wasn’t just the mess—it felt like proof I can’t handle anything anymore. I probably cry like that once or twice a week now.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Um… maybe once or twice in the past week. It’s not like I have a plan or really want to do anything—I’d never leave my baby—but late at night when I can’t sleep, the thought just flashes: “What if I weren’t here?” Then I feel awful for even thinking it.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  

<sym>Depressed mood</sym>: daily “heavy cloud,” frequent tearfulness, minimal reactivity to infant’s smile.  
<sym>Anhedonia</sym>: marked loss of enjoyment—previously pleasurable plans “feel flat.”  
<sym>Marked guilt / self-blame</sym>: attributes infant’s routine crying to personal inadequacy (“my milk isn’t good enough”).  
<sym>Generalized & peripartum-specific anxiety</sym>: daily “what-ifs,” catastrophic images of infant harm; discrete panic episodes with chest tightness and shortness of breath.  
<sym>Sleep disturbance</sym>: initial insomnia plus hyper-arousal to infant noises, averaging ~3 broken hrs/night, directly linked to ruminative worry.  
<sym>Feeling overwhelmed</sym>: describes “barely treading water,” unable to keep up with basic household tasks.  
<sym>Recurrent crying spells</sym>: ~1–2×/week triggered by minor events.  
<sym>Safety concern</sym>: passive self-harm ideation (“What if I weren’t here?”) 1–2 times in past week; denies intent or plan.  

Pattern consistent with moderate-to-severe <med>postpartum depression</med> with prominent <med>anxiety</med> features. Safety screening indicates presence of suicidal thoughts—requires immediate clinical attention for risk assessment and appropriate level of care.
